dedupe_keys.name: metropolitan area outer underground discharge channel g cans tokyo flood diversion facility performance

description: This Tokyo Metropolitan Government article describes the Metropolitan Outer Area Underground Discharge Channel, a flood control facility upstream of Tokyo run by the national ministry's Edogawa River Office, built to protect the low-lying Nakagawa and Ayase river basin where urban land grew from 5 percent in 1955 to 53 percent in 2015. Completed in 2006 after 13 years, it collects overflow from small and mid-sized rivers into vertical shafts, carries it by tunnel to a pressure-adjusting water tank, and pumps it by turbine at 200 cubic metres per second to the Edo River. The ministry estimates it is used on average seven times a year and reduced the economic effect of flood damage by about 148.4 billion yen in its first 18 years. Coverage: one basin and one facility, in a visitor-oriented article. Access: a free web page; the licence is not stated. Caveats: promotional tone, and the damage estimate method is not explained. It supports underground storage capacity and flood diversion modelling, and relates to the Copenhagen Cloudburst plan and the MWRA overflow control plan case studies in the catalogue.
